title: Review: Black body radiation (physics only); Permanent and induced magnetism, magnetic forces and fields
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for AQA GCSE Physics (8463) (review status in the bank: authored-gated-unreviewed). Questions: 4.7.1-q07, 4.7.1-q15, 4.7.1-q08, 4.7.1-q16, 4.7.1-q17, 4.7.1-q18, 4.7.1-q19, 4.7.1-q20. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Emission
items.clue: The giving out of radiation by an object.

items.label: Magnetic material
items.clue: A substance that is attracted to either pole, never repelled; iron, steel, cobalt and nickel are the ones named.

items.label: Magnetic compass
items.clue: Contains a small bar that is free to turn and line up with the field.

items.label: Perfect black body
items.clue: An object that absorbs all of the radiation incident on it, reflecting none of it and transmitting none of it.

questions.stem: Which statement gives a correct difference between a permanent magnet and an induced magnet?

options.text: An induced magnet keeps its magnetism when it is removed
A permanent magnet can only ever attract things
An induced magnet has a fixed north pole and south pole
A permanent magnet produces its own magnetic field

questions.explanation: A permanent magnet produces its own magnetic field, while an induced magnet only becomes magnetic in a field.

questions.stem: A compass is placed at a point in the field of a bar magnet. What does the direction the needle's north end points in tell you?

options.text: The straight line from that point to the nearest pole
The direction of the magnetic field at that point
The direction the compass would travel if released
The way that a south pole would be pushed there

questions.explanation: The direction of the field at any point is the direction of the force that would act on another north pole placed at that point.

questions.stem: An iron nail is brought near the south pole of a magnet and is pulled in. The magnet is then turned round so the north pole faces the nail. What happens?

options.text: The nail is still pulled towards the magnet
The nail is pushed away, as the pole has changed
The nail is pushed away only when it is close
The nail now feels no force from this new pole

questions.explanation: The force between a magnet and a magnetic material is always one of attraction, whichever pole faces it.

questions.stem: What is inside a magnetic compass?

options.text: A light piece of iron
A coil of thin wire
A small bar magnet
A drop of liquid metal

questions.explanation: A magnetic compass contains a small bar magnet, free to turn.

questions.stem: A compass is placed on a bench with no magnets anywhere near it. What does the needle do?

options.text: It settles pointing along the Earth's own magnetic field
It keeps spinning slowly, as there is no field present
It points towards the coldest part of the whole room
It points straight downwards towards the floor

questions.explanation: The Earth has a magnetic field, and the compass needle points in the direction of the Earth's magnetic field.

questions.stem: A student is plotting the field pattern of a bar magnet using a plotting compass. Which method is correct?

options.text: Slide the compass all the way round the magnet while touching it
Mark a dot at each end of the needle, then move the compass on
Draw a straight line from the compass to the nearest pole
Put the compass down and draw round the outside of it

questions.explanation: Marking both ends and moving the compass so its tail sits on the last head dot builds up one field line, which is then joined and given an arrow.

questions.stem: A student draws the field pattern of a bar magnet. Which feature of the drawing shows that the field is stronger near the poles?

options.text: The lines are drawn a long way apart there
The lines are drawn with two arrows on them
The lines are drawn closer together there
The lines are drawn longer at the poles

questions.explanation: Lines drawn closer together represent a stronger field, and they are most crowded at the poles.

questions.stem: A compass points the same way on a bench, in a field and out at sea, with no magnets nearby. What does this suggest about the Earth?

options.text: The ice at the North Pole acts like a magnet
The atmosphere is what pulls the needle
The Earth's gravity is turning the needle
The core of the Earth must be magnetic

questions.explanation: A field present everywhere with no magnet nearby must be produced by the Earth itself, which is evidence that the core of the Earth must be magnetic.
